predictions.instrument: the acceptance record's signatory against the post-occasion self-report.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often present evidence against their own decision when their rehearsal produced a recorded incapacity than when it did not.
predictions.instrument: the defence transcript, coded for self-presented counter-evidence, against the rehearsal record's incapacity field.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Decisions of *do not leave yet* will more often lack a named observer and date than decisions to leave will lack a stated ground.
predictions.instrument: both decision types coded for completeness against their respective standards.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Independent assessor levels will diverge by more than one sub-level on a noticeable share of learners, and divergence will concentrate on learners who refused to leave.
predictions.instrument: the paired independent judgements before deliberation, with divergence cross-tabulated against decision type. **If divergence concentrates on refusals, the occasion is under-specified for that decision** and the standard for a refusal needs writing, not the scale.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: Most acceptance records will omit the evidence-standard fields — observers, occasions, evidence types — or will complete them in a way that overstates what was held.
predictions.instrument: the record's fields against the observed occasion.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: The four questions after the four acts will be shortened or dropped more often than any other movement, and demonstrations in which they were dropped will produce fewer recorded incapacities.
predictions.instrument: the occasion record, coded for whether each question was asked, cross-tabulated against the not-accepting section's length. **This predicts the failure of the countermeasure §5 relies on for the control-panel operator**, and it is included because a five-minute movement at the end of a full morning is the one every timetable eats.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Learners will break the silence at least once, and most breaks will occur during the posture check rather than the deployment.
predictions.instrument: the observer's record of the author-spoke boolean and its timing. **If breaks concentrate on the last act, the cause is fatigue rather than anxiety**, and the remedy is ordering rather than instruction. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this occasion, and the programme's own position is that most predictions in this wiki will never be measured at all — which makes this register machinery rather than a result, in the sense [S068](/wiki/seminars/S068.md) establishes.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will produce at least one procedure step that a stranger cannot execute, and most of those steps will be an imperative with no object.
predictions.instrument: the procedures, coded step by step for executability by a reader without the brief, with the imperative-with-no-object form counted separately.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Answers to opening item 3 will be markedly less specific than answers to items 1, 2 and 5.
predictions.instrument: the five written answers per learner, coded *specific* / *generic* / *absent* by a second reader who does not know which item is the target.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often mark a dimension unreachable when their adversarial re-derivation disagreed with them than when it agreed.
predictions.instrument: the unreachable list against the recorded agent transcript.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners who report a lower re-derived position will place that report later in their artefact than learners reporting a higher one place theirs.
predictions.instrument: position of the finding within the document, against its direction.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will record the instrument's scan scope, cadence and latency as instructed, and then write findings that generalise beyond those bounds without noticing.
predictions.instrument: the artefacts, coded for whether any finding statement's scope exceeds the recorded scan scope. **This predicts the failure of the session's own principal countermeasure**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption. If it holds, the *therefore* sentence in exercise 4 should be moved from an exercise into the artefact's required structure.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Learners instructed to compare their item-3 answer against the criterion (exercise 3) will produce more routes-to-a-free-score in their final artefact than learners who read the same material without the comparison prompt.
predictions.instrument: a within-cohort split on whether exercise 3 was completed, against the count of self-supply and satisfiable-proxy findings in the submitted procedure. **This is the session's only direct test of the mechanism §3.6 rests on**, and a null result would mean the comparison prompt is ceremony.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: A noticeable share of learners will produce a critique of maturity instruments in place of a procedure.
predictions.instrument: the artefacts, classified as procedure, critique, or both. **If this share is large, §1 of this paper is doing the damage** and the session's opening should be moved after the workflow rather than before it. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and the prediction register of this repository is machinery rather than a result — which is [S068](/wiki/seminars/S068.md)'s finding applied to this page.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will produce at least one position whose supporting evidence is a capability rather than an act, on the first attempt.
predictions.instrument: the positions, coded per row for evidence type by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Answers to opening item 4 will more often be *nobody* than any named role, and learners answering *nobody* will more often also have produced a capability-evidenced position.
predictions.instrument: the item-4 answers coded as *named role* / *nobody* / *absent*, cross-tabulated against prediction 1's coding.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often name a role whose work got worse when their diagnosis concerned the reverted site than when it concerned a group that never started.
predictions.instrument: the item-4 answers cross-tabulated against the group diagnosed.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Where the diagnosis is a willingness problem, the proposed intervention will more often be instructional than where the diagnosis is a knowledge problem.
predictions.instrument: diagnosis and intervention coded independently and paired. **If this does not hold, the training reflex this session is built on is not present in this population** and §1 should be rewritten as a caution rather than as a premise.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will configure the group dimension correctly and then report per-group figures without stating the unattributed share.
predictions.instrument: the submitted instrumentation records, checked for whether an unattributed figure appears at all and whether it appears before the per-group table. **This predicts the failure of the session's own principal countermeasure**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption. If it holds, the unattributed share should become a required field of the artefact rather than a step of the workflow.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Learners who list unobservable groups explicitly will more often name the managed-service supplier than those who do not list any.
predictions.instrument: the unobserved list, checked for the supplier.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Learners instructed to compare their item-3 answer against the criterion (exercise 3) will more often produce a diagnosis naming a discriminating observation than learners who read the same material without the comparison prompt.
predictions.instrument: a within-cohort split on whether exercise 3 was completed, against the diagnoses coded for whether a discriminating observation is named. **This is the session's only direct test of the mechanism §3.10 rests on**, and a null result would mean the comparison prompt is ceremony. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and this repository's prediction register is machinery rather than a result — which is [S068](/wiki/seminars/S068.md)'s finding applied to this page.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: In most submissions the unpaid version will be shorter and less specific than the paid one, measured by the presence of named owners, triggers and artefacts rather than by length alone.
predictions.instrument: both parts coded for the four specificity elements, compared within submission.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners who write the unpaid version first, as instructed, will more often name an owner employed by the customer than those who report writing both together.
predictions.instrument: the named owner against the self-reported working order.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Most conflict-of-interest statements will describe the organisation's interest and omit the author's own.
predictions.instrument: the statements, coded for whose interest is named.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: In most estates the sizing model a commitment was derived from will not be recoverable, and the learners who cannot recover it will more often report it as an obstacle than as the finding.
predictions.instrument: the drift registers, coded for whether `sizing_record_found` is false and, where it is, whether the absence appears in the document's opening or in a limitations section.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will complete the drift register and stop before triggering the degradation, recording the fallback as configured rather than as observed.
predictions.instrument: the submitted registers checked against the sandbox's request logs for an actual overflow event. **This predicts the failure of the session's own countermeasure for described-rather-than-configured degradation**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption. If it holds, the triggering step should become the assessed artefact rather than a workflow step.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Learners instructed to compare their item-2 answer against the criterion (exercise 3) will more often produce an unpaid design satisfying all four specificity elements than learners who read the same material without the comparison prompt.
predictions.instrument: a within-cohort split on whether exercise 3 was completed, against the four-element coding from prediction 1. **This is the session's only direct test of the mechanism §3.9 rests on.**

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: The closing question will produce more *I do not know* answers than either alternative.
predictions.instrument: the answers, recorded verbatim and classified. **If it produces almost none, the question is being heard as a test with a correct answer** and it should be replaced rather than repeated. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and this repository's prediction register is machinery rather than a result — which is [S068](/wiki/seminars/S068.md)'s finding applied to this page.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will classify the perpetually regenerating item correctly and will still produce a note rather than a decision for it.
predictions.instrument: the findings, coded for classification and separately for whether an owner and a trigger were named.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Criterion changes will more often be proposed than costed.
predictions.instrument: the proposals, checked for whose time, against what other work, and with what maintenance expectation.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Answers to opening item 4 will more often assert what closing everything would have proved than name a route by which it could have been achieved without the estate changing.
predictions.instrument: the item-4 answers, coded *route named* / *assertion* / *absent* by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners whose closing sentence names a proposition will more often have classified all regenerated items than those whose closing sentence names a count.
predictions.instrument: the closing sentences, classified as proposition or count, cross-tabulated with classification completeness.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: Where the honest answer is that only the list improved, most learners will not say so.
predictions.instrument: the closing sentences, against an independent reading of whether anything about the system changed. **If most do say so, this session's premise about the discomfort of an unfinished list is wrong for this population** and §1 should be rewritten.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will pin both states correctly and then report a difference without having filled `detectable_difference_decided_in_advance`.
predictions.instrument: the iteration records, checked for whether that field is populated and whether it was populated before the comparison section. **This predicts the failure of the session's own countermeasure against reporting noise as a trend**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption. If it holds, the field should gate the comparison section rather than accompany it.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Most learners will report the diff between the two pinned revisions as smaller than they expected, and those who record that surprise will more often state their improvement as a proposition than as a count.
predictions.instrument: an open response at the close of the workflow, coded for whether surprise at the diff's size is reported, cross-tabulated with prediction 4's coding. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and this repository's own prediction register is machinery rather than a result — which is [S068](/wiki/seminars/S068.md)'s finding applied to this page, and which exercise 6 asks learners to demonstrate on it.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most executors will encounter at least one step they cannot perform, and most authors will not have predicted it.
predictions.instrument: the execution records against the sealed predictions, matched per step.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Answers to opening item 3 will more often predict a difficulty than name a step and a reason.
predictions.instrument: the item-3 answers, coded *step and reason named* / *difficulty predicted* / *no failure predicted* by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners will classify divergences as absent evidence more readily than as a bad rule, even where the evidence exists and the rule is at fault.
predictions.instrument: the reconciliations coded per divergence, checked against the executor's record of what they inspected.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Divergences in the flattering direction — where the executor reached a higher position — will receive shorter treatment in the reconciliation than divergences in the other direction.
predictions.instrument: the reconciliation, with treatment length and specificity coded by direction.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of lodged claims will populate the union-of-silences field with a generality rather than with a specific statement of what none of the three instruments can establish.
predictions.instrument: the lodged artefacts, with that field coded *specific* / *generic* / *absent* by a reader who has the three instrument definitions and not the claim. **This predicts the failure of the session's own principal countermeasure against treating three partial views as one complete one**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption. If it holds, the field should require one sentence per instrument rather than one for the assembly.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Counter-evidence sections will more often contain findings from the instrument the learner used least in building the claim than from the one they used most.
predictions.instrument: counter-evidence entries coded by source instrument, against the instrument distribution of the supporting evidence. **If this holds it is a finding about the search rather than about the estate** — that learners search where it is cheap rather than where the claim is weakest — and the timed search in the workflow should be re-specified per instrument.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Independent assessor levels will diverge by more than one sub-level on a noticeable share of learners, and divergence will concentrate on learners whose procedure defeated their executor early.
predictions.instrument: paired independent judgements before deliberation, cross-tabulated with the execution's stopping point. **If divergence concentrates there, the occasion cannot distinguish a bad procedure from an incomplete observation** and the standard for an early stop needs writing. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this occasion, and the programme's own position is that most predictions in this wiki will never be measured at all.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most provenance entries on a first attempt will name a person or a team rather than an observation or a record.
predictions.instrument: the ledgers, coded per row against the survives-the-person test.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often produce an observable staleness signal for items bound to a platform than for items bound to a customer's process.
predictions.instrument: the signal field, coded observable or scheduled, cross-tabulated with item type.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The retirement chosen will more often be an item of low value than the item the learner most resents retiring, despite the instruction.
predictions.instrument: the retirement, against the learner's own stated resentment ranking collected separately.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Few learners will reach for the environment-reuse parallel without prompting.
predictions.instrument: the artefacts and the session record, checked for the reference before the facilitator supplies it. **If most do reach for it, the retrieval from [S074](/wiki/seminars/S074.md) is stronger than the design assumed** and the session can afford to spend its time elsewhere.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will complete the pin block and will not use it again — no learner will re-check a pinned fact against the current head unless exercise 2 compels it, and among those who do, most will report the discrepancy as an inconvenience rather than as the finding.
predictions.instrument: the workflow record, coded for whether a pinned fact was re-checked outside exercise 2, and the learner's own written characterisation of any discrepancy found. **This predicts the failure of the session's own countermeasure**, and it is included because §8's third objection cannot be answered by argument. If it holds, the pin block is ceremony and the session should stop teaching it as discipline and start teaching it as forensics.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Ledgers will carry more rows for artefacts than for defaults — configuration values, thresholds and timeouts inherited without an owner will be under-represented relative to their presence in the repository.
predictions.instrument: a count of ledger rows by item type against an independent inventory of the same repository, taken by a second reader. **If this holds, the unprovenanced constant survives the exact instrument built to catch it**, which would mean the ledger's granularity requirement is set at the wrong level. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and no instrument named above has been applied to anybody.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most loop specifications will name a queue, a team or a system at receipt rather than a person or a role.
predictions.instrument: the specifications, coded at the receipt step.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: The reporter-return step will be the most frequently omitted of the six, despite being last in a fixed order.
predictions.instrument: the six steps, checked for completion, counted by step.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often invent a process for their own organisation than record a blank, on the first attempt.
predictions.instrument: the specifications against a follow-up question asking where each answer came from.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Most learners will identify the writing as the loop's weakest link.
predictions.instrument: the closing statements, classified by which of receipt, obligation, ownership, states, closure, return or writing was named. **If most name receipt or return, the session's premise is already held by this population** and the working movement can be shortened.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A substantial minority of learner-produced silence items will report a deliberate, explained absence — most commonly the developer reference's stated refusal to publish request and response formats — despite the categorisation block that §8's third objection claims will catch it.
predictions.instrument: the silence items, coded by a second reader as *unexplained absence with a named consequence* or *explained design decision*. **This predicts the failure of the session's own countermeasure**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Learners will attempt attribution against a public change register and, on being unable to complete it, will report that as an obstacle rather than as the result — despite exercise 4 stating that the failed check is the work.
predictions.instrument: the exercise 4 write-ups, coded for whether the incompletion is presented as a finding or as a limitation of the exercise. **This is the same reading error §9 of [WP-068](/wiki/whitepapers/WP-068.md) predicts about the failed traceability check**, and a cohort that makes it in both places has not transferred the move. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and no instrument named above has been applied to anybody.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: On a first attempt the verified class will be the longest of the four in most registers.
predictions.instrument: the registers, with entries counted by class.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Magnitudes will appear in the cited class in a noticeable share of registers, most often as a range rather than as a point.
predictions.instrument: the cited-class entries, coded for any quantity.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Undermining results will more often concern the measurement than the system.
predictions.instrument: the mandatory entry, classified by subject. **If the undermining result is nearly always about the baseline, the requirement is being satisfied by the easiest available admission** and the standard needs a second clause.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Exclusions will more often name topics than interests.
predictions.instrument: the exclusion list, coded topic or interest, against the three prompting questions.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: In the self-audit exercise, a majority of learners will place this repository's prediction register in the correct class — and a majority of the same learners will place at least one of their own engagement's activity measures in the verified class in the same sitting.
predictions.instrument: exercise 4's placement against the learner's own register, scored by the same reader in one pass. **This predicts the failure of the session's central countermeasure**, on the hypothesis that the sort is easy to perform on somebody else's material and hard on your own, which is the whole claim the session makes and the one it has never tested. **If it holds, the self-audit exercise is a comprehension check rather than a transfer instrument**, and §8's third objection is substantially correct.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Vendor-class entries will record a version and a date far more often than a silence, and the `does_not_say` field will be the most frequently empty field in the register.
predictions.instrument: the vendor entries, coded for the presence of a stated absence and of a search record. **If this holds, the class that carries the most value for the next team is the one the session's design least successfully produces.** **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and no instrument named above has been applied to anybody. **See §10.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most first-attempt amendments will be advisory in effect while being presented as binding.
predictions.instrument: the amendments, coded for whether the named mechanism can fail without a person's cooperation.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often produce an occasion for an amendment concerning an artefact they authored than for one concerning a process they were subject to.
predictions.instrument: the occasions, classified by whether the learner was author or subject.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Declined amendments will be shorter than proposed ones despite the equal-length requirement.
predictions.instrument: both, compared within submission for specificity rather than for word count.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Few learners will report a contradiction in the practice rather than resolving one silently.
predictions.instrument: the submissions, checked for a reported contradiction against the set of contradictions known to be present in the supplied practice. **If none is reported, the supplied practice does not contain a findable one** and the situation needs rebuilding rather than the session.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: Annotations at the point of change will be written when required and will not be read — no learner will cite a superseded position from this repository's own record as part of evaluating the correction that replaced it, unless an exercise compels it.
predictions.instrument: the submissions, checked for any reference to a superseded position used as evidence rather than as illustration; and, across a cohort, whether any learner's amendment cites the prior text of the clause they are changing. **This predicts the failure of the session's own countermeasure**, and it is the prediction that would most damage this design if it held, because the annotation convention is the programme's most confidently asserted and least examined practice.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners will answer opening item 4 — what looks broken and is not — with a clause whose purpose they can reconstruct from the page in front of them, rather than with one whose purpose is recorded elsewhere.
predictions.instrument: the item 4 answers, coded for whether the reason given is available on the amended page or required reading another artefact. **If this holds, item 4 is not functioning as the guard §5 claims it is**, because the control most likely to be removed is the one whose reason lives somewhere the learner did not look. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session, and no instrument named above has been applied to anybody.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most forward briefs will contain more lines claiming limitation than lines claiming unsupervised competence, and the unsupervised claims will be pitched at narrower activities.
predictions.instrument: the briefs, with lines counted by type and coded for activity granularity.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Divergence between the learner's reading and the assessors' levels will fall predominantly in the direction of learner understatement.
predictions.instrument: paired readings, with direction of divergence recorded per learner. **If divergence is predominantly overstatement, §1's account of the two pressures is wrong for this population** and the occasion's framing must be rewritten rather than its instrument.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners who engaged with divergence rather than deferring to it will more often have named an occasion in every line of their brief.
predictions.instrument: the live record coded for deferral, against the briefs coded for occasion completeness.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Answers to the fixed closing question will more often name what the learner will get wrong than who will notice.
predictions.instrument: the answers, coded for both halves.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: The double-blind lodging order will not prevent convergence: assessors who record a level before opening a brief will nonetheless revise their narrative after reading it more often than they revise their level, and the revised narratives will move towards the learner's language.
predictions.instrument: assessor narratives captured at both points, compared for level change and for lexical overlap with the brief. **This predicts the failure of the occasion's central countermeasure**, and it follows directly from §3.3's anchoring finding applied to the assessors rather than to the learner. **If it holds, the comparison measures the learner's writing and the assessors' susceptibility to it**, and the occasion's claim to measure calibration is unsupported.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Learners will place their activities at whole supervision levels rather than at sub-levels in most briefs, despite the instruction, and the sub-level distinctions will appear more often in the assessors' records than in the learners'.
predictions.instrument: both sets of records, coded for scale granularity. **If this holds, the sub-level machinery §3.2 imports is doing work for the assessors and none for the learner**, which would mean the brief's design has borrowed a scale it does not teach. **None of these has been measured, and the wider statement belongs here rather than in a footnote.** Every paper in this wiki closes with predictions naming an instrument, and not one of those instruments has been applied to anybody. No cohort has run this programme. **The design's own position, stated where it is least convenient, is that most of these predictions will never be measured at all** — and a body of work that predicts its own instrumentation will not be executed has conceded something about itself that its sources never conceded about theirs. **See §10.**

teaching_moves.text: What will your amendment be ignored in favour of? Most people produce a real occasion for 1, a workaround for 2, and an assertion for 3. Item 4 is answered with something safe. **Item 5 is answered with nothing, because it requires you to imagine your own change losing** — and it does lose, reliably, in one specific way: advisory guidance inside a system of checklists loses to the checklists. An amendment that adds good sense to a document full of gates has changed nothing while feeling like a contribution.

teaching_moves.label: The genre change
teaching_moves.text: the amendment replaces a duty with a pointer to where the duty is described. *Warning sign:* your text is shorter and refers somewhere else. **A document that migrates from stating obligations to routing readers to them gains currency and loses self-containment, and a team reading only the current version learns process rather than duty.**

teaching_moves.label: The silent correction
teaching_moves.text: the change is made and the superseded text is deleted, so the next reader inherits a position with no way to evaluate it. *Warning sign:* your amendment reads as though the clause had always said this.

teaching_moves.text: What did this programme not teach you that you will need, and how will you find out you needed it? Naming your own limits is socially cheap and most people will do it fluently. **Naming something you can be trusted with, and holding it against an assessor's contrary reading, is the act.** A brief with no line an assessor could disagree with has not been written; it has been performed. **This occasion is not a demonstration of confidence. It is a demonstration of calibration.** Understating your competence and overstating it are the same defect and are read identically, which is the thing about this occasion most learners do not believe until they are in it.
